claims.hypotheses: Algebraically closed (in particular infinite) field; regular smooth formal coordinates as used in the draft; common positive exposing weight for each finite test; finitely many polynomial/Laurent basis functions and unchanged Laurent labels.
claims.conclusion: For any finite list of nonnegative jet orders at distinct torus points, maximum output rank is at most maximum input rank, possibly at different tuples.
claims.decisive_argument: Integral mixed-jet matrix over k[[s]] specializes to the monomial matrix; nonzero minors lift; local coordinate isomorphisms and infinite-field nonvanishing return a distinct input torus tuple.

claims.hypotheses: Finite Laurent rows at z=1, with cross-degree row multiplication; integral unimodular exponent maps.
claims.conclusion: Dimension/cardinality and gradedness persist; new orders lie between zero and the real old slice length; mixed-order ranks transfer backward, and unimodular maps preserve them exactly.
claims.decisive_argument: Distinct valuation pivots, order additivity, unit shift to a polynomial of bounded degree, and the torus automorphism induced by a determinant +/-1 matrix.

source_attribution: The manuscript supplies the transfer/compression construction; the old Argus report supplies the assessed arbitrary-characteristic mixed-order reconstruction.
finite_evidence_boundary: Prime-field point maxima do not establish geometric generic maximum-rank inequalities.
qualification: Do not extend the short ledger wording to unrelated formal series or singular coordinate substitutions without the report's actual regular-coordinate/exposure hypotheses.
outside_scope: full composition without its separate hypotheses
